value.body: A wellsite geologist works at oil and gas drilling sites, describing the rocks being drilled and reporting what they mean to the drilling and exploration teams. Oilfield service companies and exploration firms hire them, usually on rotation schedules at onshore or offshore rigs. Many start as mud loggers and move up into this role.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc or M.Sc Geology / Applied Geology

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Rotational shifts at remote onshore or offshore sites

items.label: Oil and gas wells drilled in India

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most freshers enter oilfield work as a mud logger or data engineer with a service company, then move into wellsite geology after gaining rig experience. An M.Sc is commonly expected for direct entry.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading well logs and drilling data

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: operations geologist, development geologist, or petrophysics roles.
Hiring follows oil and gas exploration activity, which can be cyclical.
Rotational life means weeks away from home at a stretch.

competition.note: B.Sc (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
